newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-J&J GETS RIGHT TO RAISIO PRODUCT.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-J&J GETS RIGHT TO RAISIO PRODUCT.

text.p: Johnson and Johnson's McNeil Consumer Products unit acquired from the Raisio Group exclusive North American marketing rights to the dietary ingredient stanol ester, patented for use in reducing cholesterol. The product is marketed in Euurope in a margarine product called Benecol, and Mcneil would use it in a variety of product forms. A full text of the copany's press release follows.

FORT WASHINGTON, Pa., July 15 /PRNewswire/ -- McNeil Consumer Products, a Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) company, today announced that it has acquired from the Raisio Group (Helsinki: RTEVS) exclusive NorthAmerican marketing rights to the dietary ingre dient stanol ester, which is patented for use in reducing cholesterol. It is marketed in Europe in a margarine product called Benecol. The agreement will allow McNeil Consumer Products to use stanol ester in a variety of product forms in North America as part of a total dietary approach to managing cholesterol levels.

Stanol ester is a plant-derived substance that has the ability to inhibit the absorption of cholesterol. Naturally occurring plant sterols are already contained in small amounts in an ordinary diet. Raisio's technology enables sufficient concentrati on of stanol ester in food products to help reduce blood cholesterol.

"We are delighted to enter into agreement with McNeil Consumer Products," said Matti Salminen, chief executive, Raisio Group. "Consumers are looking increasingly to their diet as a means to improved health. McNeil's relationships with the medical co mmunity, combined with its consumer marketing expertise, will be vital to introducing this cholesterol-reducing ingredient in North America," he added.

"Europeans have responded with great enthusiasm to the Raisio Group's research and discoveries into the benefits of naturally occurring plant sterols," noted Brian Perkins, president, McNeil Consumer Products. "Americans have identified cholesterol as one of their leading health concerns, and we believe that, together with a proper diet and exercise, stanol ester opens up new possibilities for consumers to become more involved in their own health and wellness."

Since the 1950s, plant sterols have been evaluated for their ability to reduce blood cholesterol levels. The results of one major study were published in a 1995 New England Journal of Medicine article assessing cholesterol levels among 153 participan ts using Benecol for one year as part of a dietary management approach to better health. The results concluded that a diet including this product lowered total serum cholesterol levels by an average of 10.2 percent.

"The importance of diet on good health has been well documented," said Edward Nelson, M.D., Ph.D., vice president, medical/research and development, McNeil Consumer Products. "We will be working with health care professionals and researchers to determine how this ingredient can benefit the health of the nearly 100 million Americans with elevated cholesterol levels. While Finnish market results cannot be used to predict stano l ester's acceptance in North America, we are encouraged by the success Benecol has achieved in Finland thus far."
Since it was introduced in Finland in 1995, Benecol margarine has become one of the leading brands in that market, with 1996 sales of $17 million to a population of 3 million adults.
This transaction is subject to government approvals.
